observed-address-control.value: type == 'XCUIElementTypeButton' AND label == 'Address' AND visible == 1 AND accessible == 1

observed-tabs-control.value: type == 'XCUIElementTypeButton' AND name == 'TabOverviewButton' AND label == 'Tabs' AND visible == 1 AND accessible == 1

observed-toolbar-new-tab-control.value: type == 'XCUIElementTypeButton' AND name == 'NewTabButton' AND label == 'New tab' AND visible == 1 AND accessible == 1

activate.description: Bring built-in Safari to the foreground without delivering a URL, changing the selected tab, or starting WebDriverAgent.

open-url.description: Deliver one explicit HTTP or HTTPS URL through CoreDevice; Safari owns whether the normal current tab is reused or another normal tab appears.

inspect-toolbar.description: Inspect only the Address, Tabs, and New tab buttons retained from two unchanged observations of one regular-width Safari toolbar state; stop on any missing or non-unique match.

foreground-only.description: Foreground Safari only, preserving the current normal tab and allowing an existing Now page to acknowledge without URL delivery.

show-web-page.description: Foreground Safari and deliver one caller-supplied explicit HTTP or HTTPS URL exactly once.

display-now-page.description: Foreground Safari without a URL so the durable Now page gets the first bounded readiness opportunity.

recover-now-page.description: After readiness failed and only under the display router, foreground Safari and deliver the fixed local HTTP Now URL at most once.

inspect-toolbar-bounded.description: Foreground Safari and inspect only the three controls observed in the unchanged regular-width toolbar state, without page or tab mutation.

prohibited: closing any tab without separately recorded task ownership and exact current-tab identity
count-based cleanup, Close All, bulk cleanup, or closing tabs until a count matches
closing, selecting, reordering, grouping, or reading the content of any unowned or pre-existing tab
closing or repurposing the durable Now tab
entering, inspecting, selecting, creating, or closing private tabs, or crossing normal and private tab modes
continuing URL delivery or starting WebDriverAgent after CoreDevice reports the iPad locked
bypassing a local HTTP, connection-privacy, certificate, or Local Network interstitial or prompt
using a tentative selector after zero or multiple matches, or falling back to XPath or coordinates
reading history, bookmarks, downloads, saved passwords, autofill, wallet, page content, tab titles, or thumbnails outside the explicit task nonce
changing Safari, privacy, search, extension, account, tab-retention, or default-browser settings
submitting forms, downloading files, payments, account changes, destructive operations, or protected confirmations
safety.uncertain_outcome: Safari may have loaded the URL, changed history, selected another tab, or created a tab before a response was lost. CoreDevice acceptance is dispatch evidence only; inspect only the visible task nonce and ownership chain, and never replay delivery automatically.

host: Appium/XCUITest only for the single selector-discovery burst and bounded selector actions
task-owned private-LAN HTTP display server for Now recovery
device: paired physical iPad with built-in Safari
unlocked iPad for every UI action
regular-width Safari toolbar state only for bounded observation
Developer Mode only for selector discovery and selector actions
permissions: locally signed WebDriverAgent only for selector discovery and selector actions
existing Local Network access for the Now page; any prompt is a stop condition

data_access: explicit HTTP or HTTPS URLs supplied by the caller
visible regular-width Safari toolbar selector context in the authorized state
Now readiness acknowledgement handled by the local display page
data_sent: explicit URLs and normal Safari requests to destination hosts
Now readiness traffic to the task-owned private-LAN HTTP server
privacy.retention: The integration stores no tab inventory. Safari may retain normal history, website data, and tabs under existing settings; URL delivery can reuse or create persistent tab state, and exact automatic tab cleanup is unsupported.
privacy.notes: Safari is the built-in core browser. Production routes are foreground-only, explicit HTTP(S) URL delivery, and the durable Now routes. URL delivery does not establish tab ownership and may leave persistent tab state. Task-tab creation and cleanup actions are intentionally absent because exact current-task tab identity and exact cleanup are unsupported. Compatibility remains unverified.
